Predicates:
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x is taking the database course.
FromCSDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
InstructedBy(x, y) ::: x is instructed by y.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
HasPartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
Question: James has a part-time job offered by the university.
Premises:
¬∃x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x)) ::: No students who work in the library have a part-time job offered by the university.
∀x (PartTimeJob(x) ∧ Student(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students with part-time jobs offered by the university work in the library.
∀x (TakesDatabaseCourse(x) → FromCSDept(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (InstructedBy(x, y) → TakesDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students instructed by Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → InstructedBy(x, y)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by Professor David.
WorksInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
Jack ∧ ¬(PartTimeJob(jack)) ∧ ¬(WorksInLab(jack)) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Conclusion:
?
